title: 12th Standard English - Maximum Objective Questions & Official Answer Keys (2020 - 2026)
board: Tamil Nadu State Board Directorate of Government Examinations (DGE)
sections_covered: Part-I Q7-Q20: Vocabulary, Clipped Words, Blends, Compounds, Idioms, Phrasal Verbs, Modals, Tags, Prepositions, Grammar Patterns

questions.question:
Choose the correct synonym of the underlined word:
Nicola and Jacopo exhibited remarkable *demeanour* during the crisis.
questions.explanation: 'Demeanour' refers to outward behaviour or appearance and bearing.

questions.question:
Choose the correct synonym of the underlined word:
They remained *intrepid* in their efforts to support their sister.
questions.explanation: 'Intrepid' means extremely brave, courageous, or fearless.

questions.question:
Choose the correct synonym of the underlined word:
They were *resolute* in their devotion to their suffering sister.
questions.explanation: 'Resolute' means admirably purposeful, determined, and unwavering.

questions.question:
Choose the correct synonym of the underlined word:
They sold wild strawberries on the *outskirts* of the town.
questions.explanation: 'Outskirts' refers to the outer parts of a town or city.

questions.question:
Choose the correct synonym of the underlined word:
Their trade was *erratic* as they engaged in diverse casual jobs.
questions.explanation: 'Erratic' means not even or regular in pattern or movement; unpredictable.

questions.question:
Choose the correct synonym of the underlined word:
Tea is one of the *mainstays* of civilization in this country.
questions.explanation: 'Mainstay' means a person or thing on which something else is based or depends; chief support.

questions.question:
Choose the correct synonym of the underlined word:
The best manner of making tea is a subject of *violent* disputes.
questions.explanation: 'Violent' in this context means extremely intense or vehement.

questions.question:
Choose the correct synonym of the underlined word:
Tea should be poured without using a *strainer*.
questions.explanation: 'Strainer' refers to a utensil used to filter or sieve liquids.

questions.question:
Choose the correct synonym of the underlined word:
One is *curious* to see how such customs originated.
questions.explanation: 'Curious' means eager to know or learn something; inquisitive.

questions.question:
Choose the correct synonym of the underlined word:
Suffering ennobles you, makes you a better person, but it is not *solitary*.
questions.explanation: 'Solitary' means done or existing alone; isolated.

questions.question:
Choose the correct synonym of the underlined word:
The joy of living is not merely pleasure, but *amelioration* of agony.
questions.explanation: 'Amelioration' means the act of making something better; improvement.

questions.question:
Choose the correct synonym of the underlined word:
The trolley was commanded by an intrepid crew of two *maimed* children.
questions.explanation: 'Maimed' means wound or injure so that part of the body is permanently damaged; crippled.

questions.question:
Choose the correct synonym of the underlined word:
The grand prix race was a moment of sheer *ebullience*.
questions.explanation: 'Ebullience' means the quality of being cheerful, lively, and highly enthusiastic.

questions.question:
Choose the correct synonym of the underlined word:
They felt a sense of *traverse* along the razor edge ridge.
questions.explanation: 'Traverse' means travel across or through; pass over.

questions.question:
Choose the correct synonym of the underlined word:
The final climb up the rock face was *arduous*.
questions.explanation: 'Arduous' means involving or requiring strenuous effort; difficult and tiring.

questions.question:
Choose the correct synonym of the underlined word:
We gazed with *awe* at the colossal peaks around us.
questions.explanation: 'Awe' is an overwhelming feeling of wonder, reverence, or admiration.

questions.question:
Choose the correct synonym of the underlined word:
The arrival of the chair created a sensation in our *parochially* minded village.
questions.explanation: 'Parochially' means having a limited or narrow outlook or scope.

questions.question:
Choose the correct synonym of the underlined word:
He walked with an air of *splendour* after sitting on the chair.
questions.explanation: 'Splendour' refers to magnificent and splendid appearance; grandeur.

questions.prose_lesson: On the Rule of the Road
questions.question:
Choose the correct synonym of the underlined word:
Individual liberty would become universal *chaos* without social rules.
questions.explanation: 'Chaos' means complete disorder, disarray, and confusion.

questions.prose_lesson: On the Rule of the Road
questions.question:
Choose the correct synonym of the underlined word:
The traffic policeman is the symbol not of tyranny, but of *liberty*.
questions.explanation: 'Liberty' is the state of being free within society; freedom.

questions.question:
Choose the correct antonym of the underlined word:
The boys were *humble* despite their noble origin.
questions.explanation: The antonym of 'humble' (modest) is 'proud' or 'arrogant'.

questions.question:
Choose the correct antonym of the underlined word:
They led a *miserable* life after the destruction of their home.
questions.explanation: The antonym of 'miserable' (wretched/unhappy) is 'happy' or 'joyous'.

questions.question:
Choose the correct antonym of the underlined word:
They displayed *unwavering* loyalty towards their family.
questions.explanation: The antonym of 'unwavering' (steady, firm) is 'fickle', 'wavering', or 'hesitant'.

questions.question:
Choose the correct antonym of the underlined word:
Tea has *mysterious* qualities that stimulate the mind.
questions.explanation: The antonym of 'mysterious' (puzzling, obscure) is 'clear', 'evident', or 'obvious'.

questions.question:
Choose the correct antonym of the underlined word:
One should *swallow* tea with true appreciation.
questions.explanation: The opposite action of 'swallow' is to 'spit out' or 'vomit'.

questions.question:
Choose the correct antonym of the underlined word:
The addition of sugar destroys the *subtle* flavor of tea.
questions.explanation: The antonym of 'subtle' (delicate, understated) is 'harsh', 'crude', or 'obvious'.

questions.question:
Choose the correct antonym of the underlined word:
Children do not indulge in *morose* thoughts about what they have lost.
questions.explanation: The antonym of 'morose' (sullen, gloomy) is 'cheerful' or 'optimistic'.

questions.question:
Choose the correct antonym of the underlined word:
The boy suffered *malignant* tumor of the bone.
questions.explanation: 'Malignant' (cancerous/harmful) has the direct medical antonym 'benign'.

questions.question:
Choose the correct antonym of the underlined word:
Dr. Barnard witnessed an *exhilarating* spectacle in the hospital corridor.
questions.explanation: The antonym of 'exhilarating' (thrilling, energizing) is 'boring' or 'depressing'.

questions.question:
Choose the correct antonym of the underlined word:
The weather was *favourable* for the final assault on the peak.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'favourable' is 'unfavourable', 'adverse', or 'hostile'.

questions.question:
Choose the correct antonym of the underlined word:
They reached the *summit* after a long struggle.
questions.explanation: The antonym of 'summit' (highest point/peak) is 'base', 'nadir', or 'bottom'.

questions.question:
Choose the correct antonym of the underlined word:
The villagers were *reluctant* to sit on the grand chair.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'reluctant' (hesitant/unwilling) is 'willing' or 'eager'.

questions.prose_lesson: On the Rule of the Road
questions.question:
Choose the correct antonym of the underlined word:
A reasonable person will *curtail* his rights to accommodate others.
questions.explanation: 'Curtail' means reduce or cut short; its opposite is 'extend' or 'expand'.

questions.prose_lesson: On the Rule of the Road
questions.question:
Choose the correct antonym of the underlined word:
Total independence is an *insolent* claim.
questions.explanation: The antonym of 'insolent' (rude, disrespectful) is 'polite' or 'respectful'.

questions.question: Choose the clipped form of 'influenza':
questions.explanation: 'Influenza' is clipped to 'flu'.

questions.question: Choose the clipped form of 'perambulator':
questions.explanation: 'Perambulator' is clipped to 'pram'.

questions.question: Choose the unclipped form of 'chimp':
questions.explanation: 'Chimp' is the clipped form of 'chimpanzee'.

questions.question: Choose the blended word formed by combining 'smoke + fog':
questions.explanation: Smoke + fog = smog.

questions.question: Choose the components that form the blended word 'brunch':
questions.explanation: Brunch is formed from Breakfast + Lunch.

questions.question: Choose the blended word for 'medical + care':
questions.explanation: Medical + care blends into Medicare.

questions.question: Choose the combination for the blend 'electrocute':
questions.explanation: Electric + execute = electrocute.

questions.question: Choose the blended word for 'international + police':
questions.explanation: International + police = Interpol.

questions.question: Expand the abbreviation 'NEET':
questions.explanation: NEET stands for National Eligibility cum Entrance Test.

questions.question: Expand the acronym 'ISRO':
questions.explanation: ISRO stands for Indian Space Research Organisation.

questions.question: Expand the acronym 'RAM':
questions.explanation: RAM stands for Random Access Memory.

questions.question: Expand the abbreviation 'OPEC':

options.a: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries
options.b: Order of Petroleum and Energy Companies
options.c: Organization of People for Energy Conservation

questions.answer: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries
questions.explanation: OPEC = Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries.

questions.question: Expand the abbreviation 'GPS':
questions.explanation: GPS stands for Global Positioning System.

questions.question: Choose the meaning of the foreign phrase 'bonafide':
questions.explanation: 'Bona fide' is Latin for 'in good faith' or genuine.

questions.question: Choose the meaning of the French phrase 'en route':
questions.explanation: 'En route' means on the way or during the journey.

questions.question: Choose the meaning of the Latin phrase 'in toto':
questions.explanation: 'In toto' means as a whole or totally.

questions.question: Choose the meaning of the phrase 'ad hoc':
questions.explanation: 'Ad hoc' means formed or arranged for a particular purpose only.

questions.question: Choose the meaning of 'status quo':
questions.explanation: 'Status quo' means the existing state of affairs.

questions.question: Identify the grammatical structure of the compound word 'sun glasses':
questions.explanation: 'Sun' (Noun) + 'Glasses' (Noun) = Noun + Noun.

questions.question: Identify the pattern of the compound word 'dry clean':
questions.explanation: 'Dry' (Adjective) + 'Clean' (Verb) = Adjective + Verb.

questions.question: Identify the pattern of the compound word 'waterfall':
questions.explanation: 'Water' (Noun) + 'Fall' (Verb) = Noun + Verb.

questions.question: Choose the correct compound word for 'Noun + Gerund':
questions.explanation: 'House' (Noun) + 'keeping' (Gerund) = housekeeping.

questions.question: Form a derivative by adding a suitable prefix to the root word 'literate':
questions.explanation: Prefix 'il-' + literate = illiterate.

questions.question: Attach a suitable suffix to the word 'courage' to form an adjective:
questions.explanation: Courage + -ous = courageous (adjective).

questions.question: Choose the suitable prefix to form an opposite for 'legitimate':
questions.explanation: Prefix 'il-' + legitimate = illegitimate.

questions.question: Choose the meaning of the phrasal verb 'call off':
questions.explanation: 'Call off' means to cancel an event or agreement.

questions.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb to fill in the blank:
The match was ________ due to heavy rainfall.
questions.explanation: 'Called off' means cancelled due to adverse conditions.

questions.question: Choose the meaning of the phrasal verb 'put off':
questions.explanation: 'Put off' means to delay or postpone.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with suitable phrasal verb:
Firefighters worked hard to ________ the blazing fire.
questions.explanation: 'Put out' means to extinguish a fire.

questions.question: Choose the meaning of the phrasal verb 'stand by':
questions.explanation: 'Stand by' means to remain loyal to or support someone in difficulty.

questions.question: Choose the meaning of the idiom 'once in a blue moon':
questions.explanation: 'Once in a blue moon' means something that happens very rarely.

questions.question: Choose the meaning of the idiom 'burn the midnight oil':

options.b: work or study late into the night

questions.answer: work or study late into the night
questions.explanation: 'Burn the midnight oil' means to work or study late into the night.

questions.question: Choose the meaning of the idiom 'at the eleventh hour':
questions.explanation: 'At the eleventh hour' means at the very last moment.

questions.question: Choose the meaning of the idiom 'in hot water':
questions.explanation: 'In hot water' is an idiom meaning to be in serious trouble.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with a suitable modal verb:
You ________ respect your parents and teachers.
questions.explanation: 'Ought to' expresses moral duty and obligation.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with a suitable semi-modal:
My grandfather ________ walk ten miles every day when he was young.
questions.explanation: 'Used to' expresses a past discontinued habit.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with a suitable modal expressing permission:
________ I come in, Sir?
questions.explanation: 'May' is the formal modal auxiliary for seeking permission.

questions.question: How ________ you speak so insolently to your elders?
questions.explanation: 'Dare' expresses courage or boldness, commonly in 'How dare you'.

questions.question:
Add a suitable question tag:
Let's go for a walk in the park, ________?
questions.explanation: Imperative sentences beginning with 'Let's' take the tag 'shall we?'.

questions.question:
Add a suitable question tag:
She rarely visits the library, ________?
questions.explanation: 'Rarely' has a negative connotation, so it takes a positive tag 'does she?'.

questions.question:
Add a suitable question tag:
I am a brilliant student, ________?
questions.explanation: The negative tag for 'I am' in standard English is 'aren't I?'.

questions.question:
Add a suitable question tag:
Nobody called while I was out, ________?
questions.explanation: 'Nobody' is negative and plural in tag pronoun ('they'), taking positive tag 'did they?'.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with suitable preposition:
The boy was leaning ________ the wall waiting for his friend.
questions.explanation: The preposition 'against' expresses contact and physical support.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with suitable preposition:
Distribute these sweets ________ the four children.
questions.explanation: 'Among' is used for distribution among more than two individuals.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with suitable prepositional phrase:
________ his illness, he attended the annual examination.
questions.explanation: 'In spite of' shows contrast between his illness and attending the exam.

questions.question:
Complete the conditional sentence:
If I were a bird, I ________ fly across the oceans.
questions.explanation: Second conditional (unreal present: If + past subjunctive 'were', main clause takes 'would + V1').

questions.question:
Complete the conditional sentence:
If they had started early, they ________ caught the train.
questions.explanation: Third conditional (past unfulfilled: If + past perfect 'had started', main clause takes 'would have + V3').

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with suitable relative pronoun:
This is the boy ________ won the prestigious state award.
questions.explanation: 'Who' is the subject relative pronoun referring to persons.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with suitable relative pronoun:
The house ________ roof was damaged in the cyclone has been repaired.
questions.explanation: 'Whose' indicates possession for the roof of the house.

questions.question: Choose the correct syllabification for the word 'examination':
questions.explanation: 'Examination' has 5 syllables (pentasyllabic): ex-am-i-na-tion.

questions.question: Choose the word which is a 'monosyllabic' word:
questions.explanation: 'School' has only one vowel sound, making it monosyllabic.

questions.question: How many syllables are present in the word 'multiplication'?
questions.explanation: mul-ti-pli-ca-tion has 5 syllables (pentasyllabic).

questions.question:
Identify the sentence pattern:
They elected him president.

options.b: S V I O D O

questions.explanation: They (Subject) elected (Verb) him (Object) president (Complement).

questions.question:
Identify the sentence pattern:
My mother gave me a gift yesterday.
questions.explanation: My mother (S) gave (V) me (IO) a gift (DO) yesterday (A).

questions.question:
Identify the sentence pattern:
The birds are flying in the sky.
questions.explanation: The birds (S) are flying (V) in the sky (A).

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with suitable connector:
Walk fast ________ you will miss the morning train.
questions.explanation: 'Otherwise' or 'or else' expresses conditional consequence.

questions.question: He was not only an actor ________ a great philanthropist.
questions.explanation: Correlative conjunction pair: 'not only ... but also'.

questions.question: Choose the correct plural form of 'datum':
questions.explanation: Singular 'datum' becomes plural 'data'.

questions.question: Choose the plural form of 'crisis':
questions.explanation: Singular 'crisis' becomes plural 'crises'.

questions.question: Choose the plural form of 'alumnus':
questions.explanation: Singular masculine 'alumnus' becomes plural 'alumni'.

questions.question: Choose the American English equivalent of the British word 'lift':
questions.explanation: British 'lift' corresponds to American 'elevator'.

questions.question: Choose the American English word for British 'petrol':
questions.explanation: British 'petrol' is 'gasoline' or 'gas' in American English.

questions.question: Choose the British English equivalent for the American word 'sidewalk':
questions.explanation: American 'sidewalk' corresponds to British 'pavement'.

questions.question: Choose the American English word for British 'flat':
questions.explanation: British 'flat' corresponds to American 'apartment'.
